name: 1N4733A
description: 5.1V, 1W silicon Zener from the 1N4728A series, A suffix = +/-5% tolerance. Reverse-biased in breakdown as a shunt reference or clamp; common for simple rails, bias references, and overvoltage protection.
typical_application: Shunt voltage reference/regulator: fed through a series resistor from a higher rail to hold ~5.1V across the load.
gotchas: in normal use it is REVERSE biased; cathode (band) goes to the more-positive node - reversed it acts as an ordinary ~0.9V forward diode
needs a series current-limiting resistor sized for load + Izt; without it the Zener overheats and fails
5-6V is the knee where the tempco crosses zero, so 5.1V Zeners are relatively stable; lower-voltage ones drift negative
not a precision reference (5% tolerance, soft knee, noise); use a TL431 or bandgap if accuracy matters
